mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which can lead to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters signals a strong demand environment, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of instances with positive GDP growth.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decline in industrial production by more than 2% in a month indicates supply chain disruptions, which can lead to reduced output and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts combined with a decrease in retail sales signals a shift in consumer spending from goods to housing, which can lead to a reallocation of capital and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.

failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal.
